passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Every year, Mr. Qosimov told anyone who would listen that he had entered his roses in the district flower show only to please his wife. Prizes, he said, meant nothing to a man of his age. __Yet on the morning the results were posted, he was standing at the gate of the exhibition hall an hour before it opened, his good hat brushed and his hands clasped tightly behind his back.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It reveals that Mr. Qosimov cares about the competition more than he admits.
option_b: It explains why Mr. Qosimov's wife wanted him to enter the show.
option_c: It suggests that Mr. Qosimov has lost interest in growing roses.
option_d: It describes the results of the flower show.
explanation_en:
Mr. Qosimov claims prizes mean nothing to him, but the underlined sentence, starting with “Yet,” shows him arriving an hour early, dressed carefully, with hands clasped tightly, signs of eagerness and nerves. Choice A describes this function.

Choice B is wrong because the wife's reasons are never given. Choice C is wrong because his behavior shows strong interest, not a loss of interest. Choice D is wrong because the sentence describes him waiting for the results; the results themselves are not revealed.
explanation_uz:
Qosimov janoblari mukofotlar unga hech narsani anglatmasligini aytadi, ammo “Yet” bilan boshlanadigan belgilangan gap uni ko‘rgazma ochilishidan bir soat oldin, ozoda kiyinib, qo‘llarini mahkam qovushtirib turganini ko‘rsatadi — bu ishtiyoq va hayajon belgilari. A javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: rafiqasining sabablari aytilmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: uning xatti-harakati qiziqish yo‘qolganini emas, kuchli qiziqishni ko‘rsatadi. D noto‘g‘ri: gap natijalarni kutishni tasvirlaydi, natijalar oshkor qilinmaydi.

passage: For more than a century, historians accepted the account that the canal linking the towns of Bekobad and Sayhun was dug in 1847 by order of the regional governor. Historian Zarina Valiyeva noticed that the governor's own records never mentioned the project. She turned instead to the account books of local water councils, which earlier historians had dismissed as dull lists of fees. Those books show that farmers' councils raised the money, hired the diggers, and finished the canal two years before the governor took credit for it.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To criticize the regional governor for mismanaging a building project
option_b: To show how a historian used an overlooked source to revise an accepted account
option_c: To explain why water councils kept such detailed records
option_d: To argue that local records are always more reliable than official ones
explanation_en:
The text describes an accepted account, then shows how Valiyeva used account books earlier historians had ignored to reach a different conclusion about who built the canal. Choice B states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the governor is shown taking credit, not mismanaging the project. Choice C is wrong because the text does not explain why the councils kept records. Choice D is wrong because it is too extreme: the text discusses one case and makes no claim about all records.
explanation_uz:
Matn qabul qilingan talqinni bayon qiladi, so‘ng Valiyeva avvalgi tarixchilar e’tiborsiz qoldirgan hisob daftarlaridan foydalanib, kanalni kim qurgani haqida boshqacha xulosaga kelganini ko‘rsatadi. B javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: hokim loyihani yomon boshqargan emas, faqat uni o‘z nomiga yozgan. C noto‘g‘ri: kengashlar nega yozuv yuritgani tushuntirilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: haddan tashqari keskin — matn bitta holatni ko‘rib chiqadi, barcha yozuvlar haqida da’vo qilmaydi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

Anvar's first bowl collapsed on the wheel. So did the second, and the third. Each time, his grandmother simply scraped the clay away, pressed it back into a ball, and handed it to him without a word. By evening his hands ached and his shirt was gray with dust, but on the shelf by the window stood one small, lopsided bowl, and his grandmother had placed it beside her own finest work.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe the history of pottery making in Anvar's family
option_b: To explain the technical steps involved in shaping a clay bowl
option_c: To show that Anvar gives up after repeated failures
option_d: To portray a grandmother's quiet support for her grandson as he learns a difficult skill
explanation_en:
The grandmother silently helps Anvar start over after each failure and then honors his first bowl by placing it beside her finest work. Choice D captures this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the family's history is not described. Choice B is wrong because the text does not explain how to shape a bowl; it focuses on the characters. Choice C is wrong because Anvar keeps trying and finally makes a bowl.
explanation_uz:
Buvisi har bir muvaffaqiyatsizlikdan so‘ng Anvarga indamay qaytadan boshlashga yordam beradi, keyin esa uning birinchi kosasini o‘zining eng yaxshi ishi yoniga qo‘yib, uni qadrlaydi. D javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: oila tarixi tasvirlanmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: matn kosa yasash bosqichlarini tushuntirmaydi, qahramonlarga e’tibor qaratadi. C noto‘g‘ri: Anvar urinishda davom etadi va oxiri kosa yasaydi.

passage: Salt marshes flood twice a day as the tide comes in. A small marsh snail studied by ecologist Zuhra Alimova cannot breathe underwater for long, yet it thrives there. About an hour before high tide, the snails begin climbing the stems of marsh grass. They stop just above the highest point the water will reach, wait there while the marsh is flooded, and then crawl back down to the mud once the tide goes out.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe how one animal avoids being covered by rising water
option_b: To compare marsh snails with snails that live on land
option_c: To explain why tides rise and fall twice a day
option_d: To argue that salt marshes should be better protected
explanation_en:
Most of the text describes what the snail does as the tide comes in: it climbs grass stems, waits above the water, and climbs down when the tide goes out. Choice A states this purpose.

Choice B is wrong because land snails are never mentioned. Choice C is wrong because the text only notes that marshes flood twice a day; it does not explain the cause of tides. Choice D is wrong because the text makes no argument about protecting marshes.
explanation_uz:
Matnning asosiy qismi suv ko‘tarilayotganda shilliqqurt nima qilishini tasvirlaydi: o‘tlar poyasiga chiqadi, suv ustida kutadi va suv qaytgach pastga tushadi. A javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: quruqlik shilliqqurtlari tilga olinmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: matn faqat botqoqlik kuniga ikki marta suv bosishini qayd etadi, suv ko‘tarilishining sababini tushuntirmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: botqoqliklarni muhofaza qilish haqida hech qanday da’vo yo‘q.

passage: In a survey repeated every ten years since 2000, residents of the city of Sarbon have been asked whether most of their neighbors can be trusted. The share answering yes has fallen steadily, from 64 percent to 41 percent. __Over the same period, however, the share of residents who report having lent money or tools to a neighbor, or having watched a neighbor's children, has risen.__ Sociologist Nigora Abdulloyeva suggests that what has changed is less how people treat their neighbors than how willing they are to describe them as trustworthy.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It provides further evidence that trust among neighbors in Sarbon has declined.
option_b: It explains what caused the decline in the share of residents who trust their neighbors.
option_c: It gives an example of the kind of behavior that the survey's first finding describes.
option_d: It introduces evidence that seems at odds with the survey's first finding, setting up Abdulloyeva's interpretation.
explanation_en:
The survey first shows a drop in stated trust. The underlined sentence, marked by “however,” reports that helpful actions between neighbors have increased, which seems to conflict with that drop. Abdulloyeva then interprets the gap. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the rise in helpful behavior points the other way. Choice B is wrong because the sentence does not explain why stated trust fell; it presents a contrasting trend. Choice C is wrong because lending tools and watching children are signs of trust, not examples of its decline.
explanation_uz:
So‘rov avval bildirilgan ishonchning kamayganini ko‘rsatadi. “However” bilan ajratilgan belgilangan gap esa qo‘shnilar o‘rtasidagi yordam ko‘payganini xabar qiladi va bu o‘sha pasayishga zid ko‘rinadi. So‘ng Abdulloyeva bu nomuvofiqlikni talqin qiladi. D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: yordamning ko‘payishi teskari yo‘nalishni ko‘rsatadi. B noto‘g‘ri: gap ishonch nega kamayganini tushuntirmaydi, qarama-qarshi tendensiyani keltiradi. C noto‘g‘ri: asbob berish va bolalarga qarash ishonch belgisi, uning pasayishiga misol emas.

passage: City planners have usually treated public benches simply as places for people to rest. Urban planner Iroda Saidova argues that benches serve an important social purpose as well: they encourage conversations between strangers. __When her team observed 600 people using benches in three city parks, more than half spoke with someone they had not arrived with.__ Saidova recommends placing benches in pairs facing each other.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It describes the problem that Saidova's recommendation is meant to solve.
option_b: It explains why planners have treated benches only as places to rest.
option_c: It provides evidence supporting Saidova's claim about benches.
option_d: It presents a finding that challenges Saidova's argument.
explanation_en:
Saidova claims that benches encourage conversations between strangers. The underlined sentence reports that more than half of the bench users spoke with someone they had not arrived with, which supports that claim. Choice C describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the sentence describes a benefit of benches, not a problem. Choice B is wrong because it does not explain the planners' traditional view. Choice D is wrong because the finding supports Saidova's argument rather than challenging it.
explanation_uz:
Saidova o‘rindiqlar notanish odamlar o‘rtasidagi suhbatga yordam beradi, deb da’vo qiladi. Belgilangan gap o‘rindiqdan foydalanganlarning yarmidan ko‘pi o‘zi bilan kelmagan odam bilan gaplashganini xabar qiladi va bu da’voni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. C javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: gap muammoni emas, o‘rindiqlarning foydasini tasvirlaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: rejalashtiruvchilarning an’anaviy qarashi tushuntirilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: topilma Saidovaning fikriga zid emas, uni tasdiqlaydi.

passage: In nineteenth-century market towns, a merchant's reputation could matter more than a written contract. In the town of Qumtepa, for example, cloth traders regularly sold goods worth months of income on nothing more than a spoken promise to pay after the harvest. Records from the town's market court show that such agreements were rarely broken. A trader who failed to pay, after all, would find that no one in the bazaar would deal with him again.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It gives a specific example that illustrates the claim made in the first sentence.
option_b: It presents an exception to the claim made in the first sentence.
option_c: It explains why written contracts became common in later years.
option_d: It describes how the town's market court settled disputes.
explanation_en:
The first sentence claims that reputation could matter more than a written contract. The second sentence, introduced by “for example,” describes Qumtepa traders selling valuable goods on a spoken promise alone. Choice A describes this function.

Choice B is wrong because the example supports the claim rather than contradicting it. Choice C is wrong because the text does not discuss later changes. Choice D is wrong because the court records are mentioned in the third sentence, and even there the text does not explain how disputes were settled.
explanation_uz:
Birinchi gap obro‘ yozma shartnomadan muhimroq bo‘lishi mumkinligini da’vo qiladi. “For example” bilan boshlangan ikkinchi gap Qumtepa savdogarlari qimmatbaho mollarni faqat og‘zaki va’da asosida sotganini tasvirlaydi. A javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: misol da’voga zid emas, uni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: keyingi o‘zgarishlar muhokama qilinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: sud yozuvlari uchinchi gapda tilga olinadi, u yerda ham nizolar qanday hal qilingani tushuntirilmaydi.

passage: In the 1860s, surveyor Rahim Ostonov set out to make the first accurate map of the mountain roads east of his home city. He walked every route himself, counting his steps to measure distances and using a compass to record each change in direction. Where roads crossed rivers, he waded in to measure the depth of the water. His finished map, completed after six years, was used by travelers for decades.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that maps made by walking are more accurate than modern maps
option_b: To describe the methods one surveyor used to make an accurate map
option_c: To explain why mountain roads were dangerous for travelers
option_d: To compare Ostonov's map with earlier maps of the same region
explanation_en:
Most of the text explains how Ostonov made his map: walking each route, counting steps, using a compass, measuring river depths. Choice B states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because modern maps are never mentioned. Choice C is wrong because the text does not discuss dangers of the roads. Choice D is wrong because the text calls Ostonov's map the first accurate one but does not compare it with any earlier maps.
explanation_uz:
Matnning ko‘p qismi Ostonov xaritani qanday tuzganini tushuntiradi: har bir yo‘lni piyoda bosib o‘tgan, qadamlarni sanagan, kompasdan foydalangan, daryolar chuqurligini o‘lchagan. B javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: zamonaviy xaritalar tilga olinmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: yo‘llarning xavfi muhokama qilinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn Ostonov xaritasini birinchi aniq xarita deydi, lekin uni oldingi xaritalar bilan taqqoslamaydi.

passage: Music critic Akbarali Mo'minov argues that the composer Sitora Haydarova's songs owe more to the street musicians of her childhood than to the conservatory where she later trained. Her melodies use the same short, repeating phrases heard in market performances, and her rhythms follow the patterns of folk dances rather than concert music. __Some listeners might point out that Haydarova's songs are written for a full orchestra, an instrument no street musician could use; but the orchestra, Mo'minov replies, only dresses melodies whose shape comes straight from the bazaar.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It provides further evidence that Haydarova's melodies resemble street music.
option_b: It explains why Haydarova chose to train at a conservatory.
option_c: It suggests that Mo'minov has changed his view of Haydarova's music.
option_d: It addresses a possible objection to Mo'minov's argument.
explanation_en:
The underlined sentence raises a point that seems to cut against Mo'minov's claim (the songs use a full orchestra) and then gives his response (the orchestra only decorates melodies that come from street music). Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the sentence first raises a counterpoint rather than simply adding evidence. Choice B is wrong because her reasons for training at the conservatory are not discussed. Choice C is wrong because Mo'minov defends, rather than changes, his view.
explanation_uz:
Belgilangan gap Mo‘minov fikriga zid ko‘ringan dalilni keltiradi (qo‘shiqlar to‘liq orkestr uchun yozilgan) va so‘ng uning javobini beradi (orkestr faqat ko‘chadan kelgan kuylarni bezaydi). D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: gap shunchaki dalil qo‘shmaydi, avval qarshi fikrni ko‘taradi. B noto‘g‘ri: konservatoriyada o‘qish sabablari muhokama qilinmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: Mo‘minov fikrini o‘zgartirmaydi, himoya qiladi.

passage: Soil microbiologist Kamron Islomov has found that certain soil bacteria can help wheat plants survive drought. Plants grown with the bacteria wilted later and recovered faster than plants grown without them. __The effect appeared, however, only in soils that had experienced at least one earlier drought; in soils with no history of drought, plants grown with the bacteria fared no better than the others.__ Islomov suspects that earlier dry periods select for bacteria that are already adapted to water stress.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It narrows the finding by identifying the conditions under which it holds.
option_b: It presents evidence that overturns the finding described earlier in the text.
option_c: It explains the process by which the bacteria protect wheat plants.
option_d: It suggests that Islomov's experimental methods were flawed.
explanation_en:
The earlier sentences report that the bacteria help plants survive drought. The underlined sentence adds that this was true only in soils with a history of drought. It limits, but does not reject, the finding. Choice A describes this function.

Choice B is wrong because it is too strong: the finding still holds in one kind of soil, so it is qualified, not overturned. Choice C is wrong because the sentence says when the effect appears, not how the bacteria work; the possible explanation comes in the next sentence. Choice D is wrong because nothing questions Islomov's methods.
explanation_uz:
Oldingi gaplar bakteriyalar o‘simliklarga qurg‘oqchilikdan omon qolishga yordam berishini xabar qiladi. Belgilangan gap bu faqat ilgari qurg‘oqchilik bo‘lgan tuproqlarda kuzatilganini qo‘shadi. U topilmani cheklaydi, lekin rad etmaydi. A javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: juda keskin — topilma bir turdagi tuproqda baribir o‘rinli, demak u cheklangan, rad etilmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: gap bakteriyalar qanday ishlashini emas, ta’sir qachon paydo bo‘lishini aytadi; mumkin bo‘lgan izoh keyingi gapda. D noto‘g‘ri: Islomovning usullari shubha ostiga qo‘yilmagan.

passage: In a two-year study in the province of Mirzaobod, economist Shahlo Ergasheva sent free weather forecasts by text message to 1,200 farmers. Compared with farmers who did not receive the messages, those who did were more likely to delay planting before dry spells, and their wheat yields were about 8 percent higher on average. __If similar results appear in other regions, agriculture ministries could raise harvests at a very low cost simply by sharing forecasts they already produce.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It explains how the forecasts in the study were produced.
option_b: It questions whether the study's results were accurate.
option_c: It describes a problem that farmers faced before the study began.
option_d: It considers a possible broader application of the study's findings.
explanation_en:
After the study's results are reported, the underlined sentence imagines what could happen if the results hold elsewhere: ministries could raise harvests cheaply by sharing forecasts. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the sentence only notes that ministries already produce forecasts; it does not explain how. Choice B is wrong because the condition “if similar results appear” looks ahead to other regions rather than doubting the study's accuracy. Choice C is wrong because the sentence looks forward, not back to conditions before the study.
explanation_uz:
Tadqiqot natijalari keltirilgach, belgilangan gap natijalar boshqa joylarda ham tasdiqlansa nima bo‘lishini tasavvur qiladi: vazirliklar prognozlarni ulashish orqali hosilni arzon yo‘l bilan oshirishi mumkin. D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: gap vazirliklar prognozlarni allaqachon tayyorlashini aytadi, lekin qanday tayyorlanishini tushuntirmaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: “if similar results appear” sharti tadqiqot aniqligiga shubha emas, boshqa hududlarga nazar. C noto‘g‘ri: gap oldinga qaraydi, tadqiqotdan oldingi holatni tasvirlamaydi.

passage: On the north wall of an eighteenth-century house in the village of Uchqora, a painted garden scene has an odd feature: one tree seems to grow out of the middle of a doorway. Art conservator Nasiba Rajabova examined the wall with infrared light, which can reveal layers hidden beneath paint. She found the outline of an earlier doorway, later filled in, sitting exactly where the tree now stands. Rajabova concluded that the painter had covered an old doorway that had been sealed shut.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It explains how infrared light works and then lists other uses for it.
option_b: It argues that a painting has been wrongly dated and proposes a new date.
option_c: It describes a puzzling feature of an artwork, explains how a researcher investigated it, and presents her conclusion.
option_d: It compares two paintings in the same house and explains how they differ.
explanation_en:
The text begins with a puzzle (a tree growing from a doorway), explains Rajabova's infrared examination, and ends with her conclusion that the painter covered a sealed doorway. Choice C follows this order.

Choice A is wrong because infrared light is mentioned only as a tool; no other uses are listed. Choice B is wrong because the painting's date is never questioned. Choice D is wrong because only one painting is discussed.
explanation_uz:
Matn jumboq bilan boshlanadi (eshik o‘rtasidan o‘sib chiqqan daraxt), so‘ng Rajabovaning infraqizil nur bilan tekshiruvini tushuntiradi va rassom yopilgan eshikni bo‘yab yashirgan degan xulosa bilan tugaydi. C javob shu tartibga mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: infraqizil nur faqat vosita sifatida tilga olingan, boshqa qo‘llanilishlari sanalmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: rasmning sanasi shubha ostiga qo‘yilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta rasm muhokama qilinadi.

passage: __Ecologists use the term “nurse plant” for a larger plant whose shade and fallen leaves create conditions in which the seedlings of other species can survive.__ In the dry hills where ecologist Behruz Aminov works, young juniper trees almost never survive in open ground, where the summer sun dries out the soil. Aminov found that four out of five surviving juniper seedlings were growing beneath the branches of a low, spreading shrub.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It presents a claim that the rest of the text argues against.
option_b: It describes the method Aminov used in his study.
option_c: It explains why juniper trees grow slowly in dry regions.
option_d: It defines a concept that the rest of the text illustrates with a specific example.
explanation_en:
The underlined sentence explains what a “nurse plant” is. The rest of the text gives an example: juniper seedlings survive mainly in the shade of a shrub, which acts as a nurse plant. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the rest of the text supports the idea rather than arguing against it. Choice B is wrong because the sentence defines a term; it does not describe how Aminov gathered data. Choice C is wrong because the sentence says nothing about how fast junipers grow.
explanation_uz:
Belgilangan gap “nurse plant” (enaga o‘simlik) nima ekanini tushuntiradi. Matnning qolgan qismi misol keltiradi: archa nihollari asosan buta soyasida omon qoladi, ya’ni buta enaga o‘simlik vazifasini bajaradi. D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnning qolgan qismi bu g‘oyani rad etmaydi, tasdiqlaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: gap atamani ta’riflaydi, Aminov ma’lumot qanday to‘plaganini tasvirlamaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: gapda archaning qanchalik tez o‘sishi haqida hech narsa yo‘q.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

From the photographs her cousin had sent, Shirin had pictured Tashkent as a city of fountains and wide, quiet avenues. But when she stepped off the bus, the first thing she noticed was the noise: car horns, a vendor shouting the price of melons, music pouring from an open café. Someone bumped her suitcase, apologized, and hurried on. She stood still for a moment, holding the handle tightly, and laughed.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It presents a character's expectations about a place and then describes how her first experience of it differs.
option_b: It describes a character's journey and then explains why she decided to return home.
option_c: It recounts an argument between two cousins about a city.
option_d: It describes a city's history and then its present-day appearance.
explanation_en:
The text first tells how Shirin imagined the city (fountains, quiet avenues) and then describes her noisy, crowded arrival. Choice A describes this structure.

Choice B is wrong because Shirin has just arrived; nothing suggests she decides to go home. Choice C is wrong because the cousin only sent photographs; there is no argument. Choice D is wrong because the city's history is not discussed.
explanation_uz:
Matn avval Shirin shaharni qanday tasavvur qilganini (favvoralar, sokin xiyobonlar) aytadi, keyin uning shovqinli, gavjum joyga kelishini tasvirlaydi. A javob shu tuzilishni ifodalaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: Shirin endigina yetib kelgan, uyga qaytishga qaror qilgani aytilmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: amakivachchasi faqat suratlar yuborgan, hech qanday bahs yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: shahar tarixi muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: It is widely believed that people who live near green spaces are healthier. A large survey of residents in the city of Navbahor supports this belief: residents living within 300 meters of a park reported fewer days of illness than those living farther away. Public health researcher Davron Yuldashev, however, points out that homes near parks in Navbahor are also more expensive, so their residents tend to have higher incomes and better access to doctors, either of which could explain the difference.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It presents a belief, describes a study that disproves it, and then proposes a new study.
option_b: It describes two surveys that reached opposite conclusions.
option_c: It presents a belief, reports data consistent with that belief, and then offers an alternative explanation for the data.
option_d: It explains how a city decided where to build its parks.
explanation_en:
The text states a belief (green spaces make people healthier), describes survey results that fit it, and then presents Yuldashev's point that income and access to doctors could explain the same results. Choice C describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because the survey supports the belief rather than disproving it, and no new study is proposed. Choice B is wrong because only one survey is described. Choice D is wrong because the text never discusses how park locations were chosen.
explanation_uz:
Matn qarashni bayon qiladi (yashil maydonlar odamlarni sog‘lomroq qiladi), unga mos so‘rov natijalarini keltiradi, so‘ng Yuldashevning daromad va shifokorga yetish imkoniyati ham xuddi shu natijani tushuntirishi mumkinligi haqidagi fikrini beradi. C javob shu tuzilishni tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: so‘rov qarashni rad etmaydi, qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi, yangi tadqiqot ham taklif qilinmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta so‘rov tasvirlangan. D noto‘g‘ri: bog‘lar joyi qanday tanlangani muhokama qilinmaydi.

passage: Some scientists have proposed that the bright stripes on the backs of hill-stream frogs warn predators that the frogs are poisonous. Others have suggested that the stripes help the frogs blend in among sunlit pebbles. To test these ideas, biologist Feruz Salimov analyzed the frogs' skin and found no toxins. He then placed clay models of striped and unstriped frogs along a stream; birds attacked the unstriped models twice as often.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a single hypothesis and then explains why it is impossible to test.
option_b: It explains how frogs produce poison and why predators avoid it.
option_c: It presents two competing explanations and then describes evidence that favors one of them.
option_d: It describes an experiment and then explains why its results were rejected.
explanation_en:
The text gives two explanations for the stripes (warning versus camouflage), then reports that the frogs have no toxins and that striped models were attacked less, evidence favoring camouflage. Choice C describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because two hypotheses are presented, and both are tested. Choice B is wrong because the frogs turn out to have no poison. Choice D is wrong because nothing suggests the results were rejected.
explanation_uz:
Matn chiziqlar uchun ikki tushuntirishni (ogohlantirish va niqoblanish) beradi, so‘ng qurbaqalarda zahar yo‘qligi va chiziqli modellarga kamroq hujum qilinganini xabar qiladi — bu niqoblanish foydasiga dalil. C javob shu tuzilishni tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: ikki faraz keltirilgan va ikkalasi sinab ko‘rilgan. B noto‘g‘ri: qurbaqalarda zahar yo‘qligi aniqlangan. D noto‘g‘ri: natijalar rad etilgani haqida gap yo‘q.

passage: Desert spiny lizards change color over the course of a day. In the cool early morning, their skin is nearly black. Dark skin absorbs sunlight quickly, allowing the lizards to warm their bodies enough to hunt within minutes of sunrise. By midday, when the sand is hot enough to be dangerous, the same lizards have turned pale gray, reflecting much of the sunlight that strikes them.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a danger that the lizards face at midday.
option_b: It introduces a second species for comparison with the first.
option_c: It presents a question that the rest of the text leaves unanswered.
option_d: It explains how the coloring described in the previous sentence benefits the lizards.
explanation_en:
The second sentence says the lizards are nearly black in the morning. The third sentence explains why that matters: dark skin absorbs sunlight and lets them warm up fast enough to hunt. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the midday danger appears in the fourth sentence, not the third. Choice B is wrong because only one species is discussed. Choice C is wrong because the third sentence answers a question rather than raising one.
explanation_uz:
Ikkinchi gapda kaltakesaklar ertalab deyarli qora bo‘lishi aytiladi. Uchinchi gap buning nima uchun muhimligini tushuntiradi: qora teri quyosh nurini yutadi va ularga ov qilish uchun tez isinish imkonini beradi. D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: tush paytidagi xavf uchinchi emas, to‘rtinchi gapda aytiladi. B noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta tur muhokama qilinadi. C noto‘g‘ri: uchinchi gap savol qo‘ymaydi, aksincha javob beradi.

passage: When the city of Oltinsoy stopped charging fines for overdue library books in 2019, critics predicted chaos, and the first figures seemed to prove them right: the share of books returned on time fell from 91 percent to 87 percent. Economist Laziz Nurmatov looked further. He found that more than 6,000 residents who had stopped borrowing because of unpaid fines, many of them from low-income households, returned to the library within a year. As a result, the total number of books borrowed rose by 12 percent, and nearly all overdue books were eventually returned.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that every library should immediately stop charging fines
option_b: To explain why fewer books were returned on time after fines were ended
option_c: To present evidence that a policy's overall effects were more positive than one narrow measure suggested
option_d: To question the methods that Nurmatov used to evaluate the policy
explanation_en:
The text reports one discouraging figure (fewer on-time returns) and then describes Nurmatov's broader findings: thousands of former users returned, total borrowing rose, and nearly all books came back. Choice C states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because it is too extreme; the text describes one city's results and makes no recommendation for every library. Choice B is wrong because the text reports the drop in on-time returns but never explains its cause, and the drop is only the starting point. Choice D is wrong because the text relies on Nurmatov's findings rather than questioning them.
explanation_uz:
Matn bitta salbiy ko‘rsatkichni (o‘z vaqtida qaytarilgan kitoblar kamaygani) keltiradi, so‘ng Nurmatovning kengroq topilmalarini tasvirlaydi: minglab sobiq kitobxonlar qaytgan, umumiy kitob olish ko‘paygan va deyarli barcha kitoblar qaytarilgan. C javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: haddan tashqari keskin — matn bitta shahar natijalarini tasvirlaydi va barcha kutubxonalarga tavsiya bermaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: matn o‘z vaqtida qaytarishning kamayganini aytadi, lekin sababini tushuntirmaydi; bu faqat boshlang‘ich nuqta. D noto‘g‘ri: matn Nurmatov topilmalariga tayanadi, ularni shubha ostiga qo‘ymaydi.

passage: Across the streams of the Oqsoy valley, ecologist Ozoda Fayzullayeva has found that streams shaded by trees hold more species of insect larvae than unshaded streams. One stream seemed to break this pattern: although it ran through open meadow, it was nearly as rich in species as the most heavily shaded sites. Fayzullayeva discovered that the stream was fed by cold springs that kept its water as cool as a shaded stream's. Because shade benefits larvae mainly by keeping water cool, the exception, she argues, actually confirms that temperature is what matters.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It reports a pattern, describes an observation that seemed to conflict with it, and explains why that observation actually supports the reasoning behind the pattern.
option_b: It reports a pattern, describes an observation that disproves it, and proposes a new pattern to replace it.
option_c: It describes two streams in detail and argues that one is more valuable to protect.
option_d: It explains a method for measuring water temperature and then reports the results of using it.
explanation_en:
The text states a pattern (shaded streams hold more species), describes an unshaded stream that seemed to be an exception, and shows that the stream's cold springs keep it cool, so it supports the idea that cool water is what matters. Choice A describes this structure.

Choice B is wrong because the exception is explained, not used to throw out the pattern, and no new pattern replaces it. Choice C is wrong because the text discusses many streams and makes no argument about protection. Choice D is wrong because no measuring method is explained.
explanation_uz:
Matn qonuniyatni bayon qiladi (soyali soylarda turlar ko‘proq), istisno bo‘lib ko‘ringan ochiq soyni tasvirlaydi va uning sovuq buloqlar tufayli salqin ekanini ko‘rsatadi; demak u sovuq suv muhim degan fikrni tasdiqlaydi. A javob shu tuzilishni tasvirlaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: istisno tushuntirilgan, qonuniyatni rad etish uchun ishlatilmagan, yangi qonuniyat ham taklif qilinmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: matn ko‘p soylar haqida va muhofaza haqida da’vo qilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: o‘lchash usuli tushuntirilmagan.

passage: In several fifteenth-century buildings in the region around the town of Qarshigul, tile panels contain a single tile set slightly out of line with the rest. Many scholars have interpreted these misaligned tiles as expressions of humility, a reminder that only the divine is perfect. Architectural historian Munisa Tojiyeva finds a more practical explanation convincing. In every panel she examined, the crooked tile appears in the same position, the third row from the bottom, and only in buildings that records link to a single workshop. The tile, she argues, was that workshop's signature.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a building technique, explains why it was abandoned, and then describes what replaced it.
option_b: It describes an unusual feature of some buildings, presents a common interpretation of it, and then explains why one researcher favors a different interpretation.
option_c: It presents a researcher's argument and then describes evidence that other scholars have used to refute it.
option_d: It compares the work of several workshops and concludes that one produced the finest tiles.
explanation_en:
The text describes the misaligned tiles, gives the widely held “humility” interpretation, and then explains the evidence (same position, same workshop) that leads Tojiyeva to see the tile as a signature. Choice B follows this structure.

Choice A is wrong because nothing suggests the practice was abandoned or replaced. Choice C is wrong because it reverses the order and the roles: the common view comes first, and the text ends with evidence supporting Tojiyeva, not refuting her. Choice D is wrong because only one workshop is identified, and the quality of tiles is never judged.
explanation_uz:
Matn noto‘g‘ri o‘rnatilgan koshinlarni tasvirlaydi, keng tarqalgan “kamtarlik” talqinini keltiradi, so‘ng Tojiyevani koshinni imzo deb hisoblashga olib kelgan dalillarni (bir xil joy, bitta ustaxona) tushuntiradi. B javob shu tuzilishga mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: bu usul tark etilgani yoki almashtirilgani aytilmagan. C noto‘g‘ri: tartib va rollarni teskari qiladi — avval umumiy qarash keladi, matn esa Tojiyevani rad etuvchi emas, qo‘llab-quvvatlovchi dalillar bilan tugaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta ustaxona aniqlangan, koshinlar sifati baholanmaydi.

passage: Why do the male rock lizards of the Nurota foothills bob their heads up and down so often? Biologist Akmal Hamroyev suspected that the bobbing warns rival males to stay away. To test this idea, he placed a small robotic lizard that bobbed its head near the burrows of thirty males. Most of the real lizards responded by bobbing back and retreating, which supported his hypothesis.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a behavior and then explains why scientists have stopped studying it.
option_b: It compares the behavior of two kinds of lizards.
option_c: It presents two competing explanations and then rejects both of them.
option_d: It poses a question, describes an experiment designed to answer it, and reports the result.
explanation_en:
The text opens with a question about head bobbing, describes Hamroyev's experiment with a robotic lizard, and reports that the result supported his hypothesis. Choice D follows this order.

Choice A is wrong because nothing suggests scientists have stopped studying the behavior. Choice B is wrong because only one kind of lizard is discussed. Choice C is wrong because only one explanation is offered, and it is supported, not rejected.
explanation_uz:
Matn bosh qimirlatish haqidagi savol bilan boshlanadi, keyin Hamroyevning robot kaltakesak bilan tajribasini tasvirlaydi va natija uning farazini tasdiqlaganini aytadi. D javob shu tartibga mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: olimlar bu xatti-harakatni o‘rganishni to‘xtatgani aytilmagan. B noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta kaltakesak turi muhokama qilinadi. C noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta tushuntirish berilgan va u rad etilmagan, tasdiqlangan.

passage: Historian Jamshid Rahmatov argues that *Navo*, a weekly newspaper published in the town of Jizzakobod in the 1890s, did more than any official decree to win public support for a new railway line. __Granted, the paper's circulation was small: fewer than 2,000 copies were printed each week.__ But Rahmatov points out that copies were read aloud in teahouses and passed from hand to hand, so each issue likely reached many times that number of people.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It provides the strongest evidence for Rahmatov's argument about the newspaper's influence.
option_b: It acknowledges a fact that might seem to weaken Rahmatov's argument, which the text then addresses.
option_c: It shows that Rahmatov's argument about the newspaper is mistaken.
option_d: It explains why the newspaper was founded in the 1890s.
explanation_en:
“Granted” signals a concession: a small circulation seems to cut against the claim that the paper was highly influential. The next sentence (“But…”) answers this by explaining that each copy reached many readers. Choice B describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because a small circulation, on its own, works against the argument rather than supporting it. Choice C is wrong because it is too strong: the text goes on to defend the argument, so the concession does not show it is mistaken. Choice D is wrong because the sentence is about circulation, not the paper's origins.
explanation_uz:
“Granted” (to‘g‘ri, tan olish kerak) yon berishni bildiradi: kichik tiraj gazeta juda ta’sirli bo‘lgan degan da’voga zid ko‘rinadi. Keyingi gap (“But…”) bunga javob beradi: har bir nusxa ko‘plab o‘quvchiga yetib borgan. B javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: kichik tiraj o‘z-o‘zidan da’voni qo‘llab-quvvatlamaydi, aksincha unga qarshi ishlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: juda keskin — matn keyin da’voni himoya qiladi, demak yon berish uni noto‘g‘ri deb ko‘rsatmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: gap gazetaning kelib chiqishi haqida emas, tiraji haqida.

passage: In 1908 the town of Yashilobod opened its first public bathhouse with heated water. Town officials expected it to be used mostly during the cold winter months. __In fact, the bathhouse was busiest in summer, when farm workers came in from the dusty fields at the end of each day.__ Within a few years, the town had extended the bathhouse's summer hours.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It explains why officials decided to build the bathhouse.
option_b: It presents a result that differed from what officials had expected.
option_c: It describes how the bathhouse's water was heated.
option_d: It suggests that the bathhouse was too small for the town.
explanation_en:
The sentence before the underlined one states the officials' expectation (mostly winter use). The underlined sentence, beginning with “In fact,” reports that the bathhouse was actually busiest in summer. Choice B describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because the reason for building the bathhouse is not discussed. Choice C is wrong because the sentence is about who used the bathhouse and when, not how the water was heated. Choice D is wrong because nothing says the building was too small; the town extended its hours, not its size.
explanation_uz:
Belgilangan gapdan oldingi gap amaldorlarning kutganini (asosan qishda foydalanish) bildiradi. “In fact” bilan boshlanadigan belgilangan gap esa hammom aslida yozda eng gavjum bo‘lganini xabar qiladi. B javob aynan shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: hammom nega qurilgani muhokama qilinmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: gap suv qanday isitilgani haqida emas, kim va qachon foydalangani haqida. D noto‘g‘ri: bino kichikligi aytilmagan; shahar binoni emas, ish vaqtini kengaytirgan.

passage: Biologist Sevara Usmonova wanted to know whether city pigeons can tell people apart. For two weeks, one researcher shooed pigeons away from a feeding area while another, wearing a different-colored coat, simply stood nearby. Later, the birds fled from the first researcher even when both had swapped coats. __The study took place in only one park, and pigeons elsewhere may behave differently.__ Still, Usmonova argues, the results suggest that pigeons recognize individual humans by features other than clothing.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It acknowledges a limitation of the study before the text restates what the study suggests.
option_b: It presents evidence that contradicts the study's main finding.
option_c: It explains why Usmonova chose to work in a single park.
option_d: It describes the next experiment Usmonova plans to conduct.
explanation_en:
After the results are described, the underlined sentence admits that the study covered only one park, so the findings might not apply everywhere. The next sentence begins with “Still,” and restates what the results suggest. Choice A captures this function.

Choice B is wrong because the sentence does not contradict the finding; it only notes that the finding may not generalize. Choice C is wrong because no reason for choosing one park is given. Choice D is wrong because no future experiment is mentioned.
explanation_uz:
Natijalar tasvirlangach, belgilangan gap tadqiqot faqat bitta bog‘da o‘tkazilganini, demak natijalar hamma joyga taalluqli bo‘lmasligi mumkinligini tan oladi. Keyingi gap “Still” (shunga qaramay) bilan boshlanib, natijalar nimani ko‘rsatishini yana ta’kidlaydi. A javob shu vazifani ifodalaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: gap topilmaga zid emas, faqat uni umumlashtirib bo‘lmasligi mumkinligini aytadi. C noto‘g‘ri: bitta bog‘ nega tanlangani aytilmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: kelgusi tajriba haqida gap yo‘q.

passage: In 2022, public libraries in the city of Guliston began lending tools as well as books. Residents with a library card can now borrow drills, ladders, sewing machines, and garden tools for up to a week at no cost. In the program's first year, more than 9,000 tools were borrowed, and nearly a third of the borrowers had never used the library before.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that libraries should stop lending books
option_b: To explain how to repair common household tools
option_c: To describe a library program and some early signs of its success
option_d: To compare the costs of buying and borrowing tools
explanation_en:
The text explains what the tool-lending program is and then reports its first-year results: 9,000 tools borrowed and many new library users. Choice C states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the libraries lend tools “as well as books.” Choice B is wrong because nothing is said about repairing tools. Choice D is wrong because the text notes that borrowing is free but does not compare it with the cost of buying.
explanation_uz:
Matn asboblarni qarzga berish dasturi nima ekanini tushuntiradi, keyin birinchi yil natijalarini keltiradi: 9 000 dan ortiq asbob olingan va ko‘plab yangi foydalanuvchilar paydo bo‘lgan. C javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: kutubxonalar asboblarni kitoblar “bilan birga” beradi. B noto‘g‘ri: asboblarni ta’mirlash haqida gap yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: matn qarz olish bepul ekanini aytadi, lekin sotib olish narxi bilan taqqoslamaydi.

passage: The cracks in a large ice shelf studied by glaciologist Dildora Mahmudova widen each summer, but the cause has been debated. Some researchers blame meltwater that pools on the surface and seeps down into the cracks; others point to warmer ocean water eroding the shelf from below. Mahmudova placed sensors both on the surface and beneath the shelf for five summers. The cracks widened most in the summers when the ocean was warmest, including one cool summer with almost no surface melt.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To argue that the ice shelf studied by Mahmudova will soon collapse
option_b: To describe the design of the sensors Mahmudova used
option_c: To explain how a researcher distinguished between two possible causes of an observed change
option_d: To show that surface meltwater has no effect on ice shelves anywhere
explanation_en:
The text presents two competing explanations for the widening cracks, describes Mahmudova's sensors above and below the shelf, and reports results pointing to ocean warmth. Choice C states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the text makes no prediction about collapse. Choice B is wrong because the sensors are mentioned only as part of the method; their design is not described. Choice D is wrong because it is too extreme and too broad: the results concern one shelf and suggest ocean water matters more there, not that meltwater never has any effect.
explanation_uz:
Matn yoriqlar kengayishining ikki raqobatdosh tushuntirishini keltiradi, Mahmudovaning muz ustidagi va ostidagi sensorlarini tasvirlaydi va okean iliqligiga ishora qiluvchi natijalarni xabar qiladi. C javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda muz qatlami qulashi haqida bashorat yo‘q. B noto‘g‘ri: sensorlar faqat usulning bir qismi sifatida tilga olingan, tuzilishi tasvirlanmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: juda keskin va keng — natijalar bitta muz qatlamiga tegishli va u yerda okean suvi muhimroq ekanini ko‘rsatadi, erigan suv hech qayerda ta’sir qilmaydi demaydi.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

I have never cared for praise. When the mayor called my bridge design the finest in the province, I merely nodded, though I could have pointed out several features he had failed to notice. When my portrait was hung in the town hall, I asked only that it be moved to a wall with better light. __No one, I have always believed, is less given to boasting than I am.__
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It confirms that the narrator's modesty is genuine, as the earlier examples have shown.
option_b: It introduces a new subject that the narrator will go on to discuss.
option_c: It explains why the townspeople admire the narrator so much.
option_d: It ironically reveals that the narrator lacks the self-awareness he claims to have.
explanation_en:
The narrator says he does not care for praise, yet his examples show the opposite: he wanted to point out more features the mayor missed and asked for his portrait to have better light. Ending with a boast about not boasting creates irony, showing that he does not see himself clearly. Choice D describes this function.

Choice A is wrong because it reverses the effect: the earlier examples undercut, rather than show, his modesty. Choice B is wrong because the sentence sums up the narrator's self-image rather than turning to a new subject. Choice C is wrong because the text shows the narrator's view of himself, not why others admire him; the mayor's praise is of his bridge design, and the sentence says nothing about townspeople.
explanation_uz:
Hikoyachi maqtovga befarqligini aytadi, ammo misollar buning teskarisini ko‘rsatadi: u hokim payqamagan yana bir nechta jihatni ko‘rsatmoqchi bo‘lgan va portretini yorug‘roq devorga ko‘chirishni so‘ragan. Maqtanmasligi bilan maqtanish kinoya hosil qiladi va u o‘zini to‘g‘ri ko‘ra olmasligini ochib beradi. D javob shu vazifani tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: ta’sirni teskari qiladi — oldingi misollar uning kamtarligini ko‘rsatmaydi, aksincha shubha ostiga qo‘yadi. B noto‘g‘ri: gap yangi mavzuga o‘tmaydi, hikoyachining o‘zi haqidagi tasavvurini xulosalaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matn boshqalar nega uni hurmat qilishini emas, uning o‘zi haqidagi fikrini ko‘rsatadi; gapda shahar aholisi haqida hech narsa yo‘q.

passage: For centuries, families in the village of Chorbog wove carpets from wool dyed with plants gathered in the nearby hills: madder root for red, pomegranate rind for yellow. In the twentieth century, cheaper factory dyes replaced these plant dyes, and by 1980 only two weavers in the village still knew the old recipes. In 2015, a group of young weavers began recording those recipes and teaching them in free weekend classes.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It argues that factory dyes produce brighter colors than plant dyes.
option_b: It describes a traditional craft practice, explains why it nearly disappeared, and then describes an effort to revive it.
option_c: It compares the carpets of Chorbog with those of other villages.
option_d: It describes how a single carpet is woven from start to finish.
explanation_en:
The text first describes the traditional plant dyes, then explains that cheaper factory dyes replaced them until only two weavers knew the recipes, and finally describes young weavers recording and teaching the recipes. Choice B follows this order.

Choice A is wrong because the text never compares the brightness of the dyes. Choice C is wrong because no other villages are mentioned. Choice D is wrong because the text is about dyes over time, not the steps of weaving one carpet.
explanation_uz:
Matn avval an’anaviy o‘simlik bo‘yoqlarini tasvirlaydi, keyin arzon zavod bo‘yoqlari ularni siqib chiqargani va retseptlarni faqat ikki to‘quvchi bilib qolganini tushuntiradi, oxirida yosh to‘quvchilar retseptlarni yozib olib, o‘rgatayotganini aytadi. B javob shu tartibga mos.

A noto‘g‘ri: bo‘yoqlarning yorqinligi taqqoslanmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: boshqa qishloqlar tilga olinmagan. D noto‘g‘ri: matn bitta gilam to‘qish bosqichlari haqida emas, vaqt o‘tishi bilan bo‘yoqlar haqida.

passage:
The following text is from a short story.

When Gulbahor was twelve, she thought her mother's sewing was the dullest thing in the world: the same hum of the machine every evening, the same pins held between her lips. Now, years later, Gulbahor sat at that machine herself, trying to rescue a wedding dress that a customer needed by morning. Her seams wandered; the silk slid away from the needle. By midnight she understood that what had looked like a dull routine had been a kind of mastery, the work of hands that had made ten thousand seams before.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To explain the steps involved in repairing a wedding dress
option_b: To convey a character's growing appreciation for a skill she once dismissed
option_c: To describe a conflict between a mother and daughter over a family business
option_d: To show that Gulbahor decides to give up sewing
explanation_en:
As a child, Gulbahor found her mother's sewing dull; struggling with the dress, she realizes it was “a kind of mastery.” Choice B captures this change.

Choice A is wrong because the text describes Gulbahor's struggle, not a set of repair steps. Choice C is wrong because there is no conflict between mother and daughter; the mother does not even appear in the present-day scene. Choice D is wrong because the text ends with a realization, not a decision to quit.
explanation_uz:
Bolaligida Gulbahor onasining tikuvchiligini zerikarli deb bilgan; ko‘ylak bilan qiynalib, u buning “o‘ziga xos mahorat” ekanini anglaydi. B javob shu o‘zgarishni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn ta’mirlash bosqichlarini emas, Gulbahorning qiyinchiligini tasvirlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: ona va qiz o‘rtasida nizo yo‘q, ona hozirgi sahnada umuman ko‘rinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn tikuvchilikdan voz kechish qarori bilan emas, anglash bilan tugaydi.

passage: Many songbirds migrate at night, and scientists have long assumed that they do so mainly to avoid hawks and other predators that hunt by day. Ornithologist Elyor Jurayev offers a different explanation. Using tiny sensors attached to warblers, he found that the birds lose far less water flying in cool night air than in the heat of the day. Because the birds cannot drink during long flights over deserts, Jurayev argues, avoiding dehydration may matter more than avoiding predators.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
option_a: To describe the sensors that scientists use to track migrating birds
option_b: To present a finding that challenges a common explanation for why some birds migrate at night
option_c: To argue that hawks pose little threat to songbirds
option_d: To explain why warblers migrate across deserts
explanation_en:
The text states a long-held assumption (night migration avoids predators) and then describes Jurayev's findings, which suggest that avoiding water loss may matter more. Choice B states this purpose.

Choice A is wrong because the sensors are only a detail of Jurayev's method. Choice C is wrong because it is too extreme: Jurayev suggests dehydration “may matter more,” not that hawks are harmless. Choice D is wrong because the text does not explain why the birds cross deserts; it explains why they fly at night.
explanation_uz:
Matn uzoq yillik taxminni (tungi parvoz yirtqichlardan saqlanish uchun) bayon qiladi, so‘ng Jurayevning suvsizlanishdan saqlanish muhimroq bo‘lishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatuvchi topilmalarini tasvirlaydi. B javob shu maqsadni ifodalaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: sensorlar Jurayev usulining bir tafsiloti xolos. C noto‘g‘ri: haddan tashqari keskin — Jurayev suvsizlanish “muhimroq bo‘lishi mumkin” deydi, qirg‘iylar zararsiz demaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: matn qushlar nega cho‘l ustidan uchishini emas, nega tunda uchishini tushuntiradi.

passage: Many parents and school officials assume that making the school day longer will raise students' test scores. Economist Nodir Hakimov tested this idea by comparing forty schools, half of which had added an hour to their daily schedule. He found that the extra hour made no difference to scores in most schools. Scores rose only in schools that used the added time for tutoring in small groups.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
option_a: It describes a study and then explains why its methods were flawed.
option_b: It lists several benefits of a longer school day.
option_c: It presents a common assumption and then describes research showing that the assumption holds only under a certain condition.
option_d: It compares the views of two economists on how schools should use their time.
explanation_en:
The text opens with an assumption (a longer day raises scores), then describes Hakimov's study, which found that scores rose only when the extra time was used for small-group tutoring. Choice C describes this structure.

Choice A is wrong because the text never criticizes the study's methods. Choice B is wrong because the text reports that a longer day usually made no difference; it does not list benefits. Choice D is wrong because only one economist is discussed.
explanation_uz:
Matn taxmin bilan boshlanadi (uzunroq o‘quv kuni ballarni oshiradi), keyin Hakimovning tadqiqoti tasvirlanadi: ballar faqat qo‘shimcha vaqt kichik guruhlarda repetitorlik uchun ishlatilganda oshgan. C javob shu tuzilishni tasvirlaydi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn tadqiqot usullarini tanqid qilmaydi. B noto‘g‘ri: matnga ko‘ra uzunroq kun odatda farq qilmagan; foydalar sanab o‘tilmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: faqat bitta iqtisodchi muhokama qilinadi.

passage: Most mushrooms in temperate forests appear after a period of heavy rain, when the soil is damp. __A species studied by mycologist Lola Rasulova, however, produces mushrooms mainly in dry years, sometimes within weeks of a forest fire.__ Rasulova suspects that the heat of a fire or the chemicals released by burned wood may trigger the fungus to fruit.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
option_a: It introduces an exception to the general pattern described in the previous sentence.
option_b: It provides an additional example of the pattern described in the previous sentence.
option_c: It explains why forest fires have become more frequent.
option_d: It presents evidence that Rasulova's suspicion is incorrect.
explanation_en:
The first sentence says most mushrooms appear after rain. The underlined sentence, signaled by “however,” describes a species that fruits mainly in dry years. Choice A identifies it as an exception.

Choice B is wrong because the species does the opposite of the general pattern, so it is not another example of it. Choice C is wrong because the text does not discuss how often fires occur. Choice D is wrong because the underlined sentence sets up Rasulova's suspicion; it does not challenge it.
explanation_uz:
Birinchi gapda ko‘pchilik qo‘ziqorinlar yomg‘irdan keyin paydo bo‘lishi aytiladi. “However” bilan ajratilgan belgilangan gap esa asosan qurg‘oqchil yillarda meva beradigan turni tasvirlaydi. A javob uni istisno deb to‘g‘ri belgilaydi.

B noto‘g‘ri: bu tur umumiy qonuniyatning teskarisini qiladi, shuning uchun u qonuniyatga yana bir misol emas. C noto‘g‘ri: yong‘inlar qanchalik tez-tez bo‘lishi muhokama qilinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: belgilangan gap Rasulovaning taxminiga zamin yaratadi, unga qarshi chiqmaydi.
